## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}

# Count each option independently for a choose-all-that-apply column
  multi_summary <- function(var, labels = NULL) {
    x <- as.character(final[[var]])
    n_total <- length(x)
  
    # Split "1,5,6" into c("1","5","6") for each participant
    split_list <- strsplit(x, ",")
    split_list <- lapply(split_list, trimws)
  
    # Count participants selecting each code (unique() guards against duplicates)
    codes <- unlist(lapply(split_list, unique))
    tab <- table(codes)
  
    # Sort numerically
    tab <- tab[order(as.numeric(names(tab)))]
  
    data.frame(
      Variable = var,
      Category = if (is.null(labels)) names(tab) else labels[names(tab)],
      Value = sprintf("%.0f (%.1f%%)", as.numeric(tab), 100 * as.numeric(tab) / n_total)
    )
  }
  
  gender_labels <- c(
    "1"  = "Man",
    "5"  = "Woman",
    "6"  = "Transgender",
    "7"  = "Gender non-conforming",
    "8"  = "Nonbinary",
    "9"  = "Genderfluid",
    "10" = "Genderqueer",
    "11" = "Other gender identity:",
    "17" = "Prefer not to answer"
  )
  
  race_labels <- c(
  "1" = "American Indian or Alaska Native",
  "2" = "Asian",
  "3" = "Black or African American",
  "4" = "Hispanic or Latino",
  "5" = "Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander",
  "6" = "White",
  "7" = "Two or More Races",
  "8" = "Prefer not to answer"
  )
  
  # Age: mean, SD, range
  final <- as.data.frame(final)
  final$age <- as.numeric(final$age)   # convert text to numbers
  
  age_summary <- data.frame(
    Variable = "Age",
    Category = "Mean (SD); Range",
    Value = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f); %.0f-%.0f",
                    mean(final$age, na.rm = TRUE),
                    sd(final$age, na.rm = TRUE),
                    min(final$age, na.rm = TRUE),
                    max(final$age, na.rm = TRUE))
  )
  
  cat_summary <- function(var) {
    if (!var %in% names(final)) {
      warning("Column not found: ", var)
      return(NULL)
    }
    tab <- table(final[[var]], useNA = "ifany")
    data.frame(
      Variable = var,
      Category = names(tab),
      Value = sprintf("%.0f (%.1f%%)", as.numeric(tab), 100 * as.numeric(tab) / sum(tab))
    )
  }

result <- rbind(
  age_summary,
  cat_summary("sex"),
  multi_summary("gender", gender_labels),
  multi_summary("race_ethnicity", race_labels)
)

print(result, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
